items.title: Democrats secure a historic majority, and climate talks break down: Weekend Rundown
items.excerpt: Nov. 22, 2026, 6:00 PM EST By Mark Hodge, Kayla Hayempour and Tom Gottlieb Democrat Chuck Hubbard has defeated GOP Rep. Virginia Foxx for a congressional seat in North Carolina, NBC News projects, adding to a Democratic wave that is projected to deliver the party at least 258 House seats. It’s the largest House majority that any party has held this century, according to the Office of the House Historian. It’s also the largest Democratic majority since 1992, when the party also won 258 seats. The party cemented control of the chamber not only by winning competitive races in battleground districts, but also by winning in deeply Republican areas that voted for President Donald Trump by double-digit margins just two years ago. In 2024, Trump won Foxx’s district by almost 18 percentage points, per an NBC News Decision Desk analysis. See the live U.S. House election results here, with four races still to be called. ## COP31 climate talks break down after angry dispute over fossil fuels COP31 president and Turkey's environment minister Murat Kurum said Sunday that a deal had not been reached. Yasin Akgul / AFP via Getty International climate talks in Turkey broke down Sunday after the European Union and other nations rejected a draft agreement that had cut all references to fossil fuels. Negotiations fell apart two days after the United Nations’ COP31 conference was meant to end, after delegates from 196 countries and the European Union struggled to agree on new pledges for climate action and how to deliver on previous promises. COP31 President Murat Kurum said Sunday that there would be no new climate agreement draft after a fourth draft was rejected. “There is nothing to do. We did all that we could,” said Kurum, who is host nation Turkey’s environment minister. “​We will not ​be carrying out ​work on a new ⁠text in an environment ⁠where there ​is no consensus.” ... Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, D-Mich., said Sunday that he’s open to working with President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance to bring down costs and improve healthcare for Americans.

items.title: Inflation, economic growth and the mood of U.S. consumers in focus this week
items.excerpt: By Damian J. Troise - Associated Press - Sunday, November 22, 2026 NEW YORK — Inflation has become the current that runs through almost all corners of the U.S. economy and there will be more on that front this week. A key report on inflation will headline a holiday-shortened week, along with a look at the latest gauge of consumer confidence. High prices on everything from groceries to gasoline are changing consumer behavior and there is pressure on policy makers to act. The data on prices arrives ahead of the next meeting of rate-setters at the Federal Reserve, the unofficial start of the holiday shopping season, as well as Thanksgiving, which may be uncomfortably expensive this year given rising prices for food. Here’s a look at some of the key reports coming in the week ahead. ### U.S. consumer confidence is being tested Business group The Conference Board on Tuesday will release its consumer confidence survey for November. Economists expect it to show that confidence remains low as inflation puts more pressure on budgets. Overall, consumer confidence is down sharply from two years ago. The wide-ranging and unpredictable U.S. trade war with much of the world prompted price increases and made planning ahead difficult for both consumers and businesses. The U.S. war with Iran that started in 2026 fueled inflation throughout the year by curtailing the flow of oil through the Strait of Hormuz and raising energy prices. Higher prices for oil and gasoline boosted shipping costs for a wide range of goods. The high cost of energy, goods and services has been notably referenced by write-in responses to the monthly consumer confidence surveys. ### Inflation data could tip balance toward higher borrowing costs A inflation update is expected to provide more details on what most Americans know - things have become expensive. The U.S. will release the October personal consumption expenditures report, or PCE, on Wednesday. The data carries a lot of weight because it is the preferred measure of inflation used by the Federal Reserve, which is attempting to bring inflation down to its target rate of 2%. Inflation has been rising at a sharp rate since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran early this year fueling a surge in energy prices. Higher gasoline prices have eaten up a bigger portion of household budgets. Higher costs for shipping and warehousing goods because of soaring diesel prices are leaching into the broader economy. The Fed’s main tool in fighting inflation is raising interest rates and that makes something else more expensive - borrowing money. The central bank is expected to raise its benchmark interest rate at its next meeting to cool down the economy. It’s a tough balancing act because the Fed’s other mandate is maximum employment. Higher rates can make employers less likely to hire. ### The U.S. economy is motoring along The U.S. Department of Commerce on Wednesday will release an update on the nation’s economic growth during the third quarter. The first read showed gross domestic product grew at 3.4% during the third quarter. GDP is a measure of the nation’s output of goods and services. The economy has proven resilient despite inflation. Economic growth accelerated from the 2.2% increase in the second quarter. Much of that growth has been driven by an AI investment boom, but that is a sector that has been rattled in recent weeks. The tech-heavy Nasdaq tumbled more than 8% last week, with particularly sharp declines to end the week. ### Low-hire, low-fire employment in the U.S. The latest weekly update on unemployment claims, which are a proxy for layoffs, will be released Wednesday in a scheduling shift ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. Economists watch this weekly report closely because it can provide signals about where the job market is headed. Claims have remained at historically low levels amid a broader jobs market that has remained a strong point in an economy pressured by rising inflation. Layoffs remain modest by historic standards.

items.title: Trump moves to restrict congressional oversight of contractors
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump has directed federal contractors to seek permission from the White House before complying with congressional requests for information, the latest effort by the administration to blunt Democratic investigative plans next year. In an executive order issued Friday, Trump ordered contractors and subcontractors to coordinate responses to congressional queries with the White House, and to withhold information that the administration deems confidential or protected under “executive privilege.” Firms that fail to comply could have their contracts suspended or terminated, according to the order. “The ability of the Congress to seek executive branch information is limited,” the order states. “It cannot seek information from executive branch departments and agencies, employees, or federal contractors without a valid legislative purpose that does not intrude on core executive functions.” The move comes as Democrats, who will take control of the House and Senate next year, plan to cast a wide net in investigating everything from the administration’s policies to any conflicts of interest it has had. This past week, Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the top Democrat on the Oversight and Government Reform Committee, sent a dozen notices to members of Trump’s family, Vice President JD Vance, and other current and former administration officials asking them to preserve documents on a host of issues. Democrats have made clear that they intend to investigate no-bid contracts, and how alleged pay-to-play schemes might have influenced contracting decisions. Rep. Jamie Raskin (D., Md.), who is expected to lead the Judiciary Committee, called the order “blatantly unlawful.” And Sen. Maggie Hassan (D., N.H.), who is poised to be the chair of the Homeland Security Committee, said in her own statement that “every federal contractor should know that this executive order does not override their obligation to comply with congressional requests for information or subpoenas.” She added: “Congress will get the information that it needs, and, if necessary, we will use every authority available to us to get it.” ... Will Scharf, the White House counsel, sent a letter to Democrats on congressional committees saying that the White House would not respond to oversight requests until they took control of Congress in January. items.title: House Democrats split over risking lame-duck shutdown to defund Iran war
items.excerpt: House Democrats are wrestling with a lame-duck strategy on the Iran war, divided over whether to demand an end to war funding, which could risk triggering a government shutdown — or punting that fight to next year, when they’ll control Congress. On one side of the debate are liberals who, emboldened by this month’s midterm landslide, want to use the Democrats’ leverage in the government funding battle to deny the Pentagon any more money to conduct the war. “We’re going to fight to get that Iran funding removed for offensive military capability,” said Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.). On the other side are top Democrats, including the lead negotiators on the spending package, who also oppose the war but aren’t ready to shutter the government over defunding it. “I frankly want to … end the funding to the Iran War. But shutting the government down doesn’t stop the war,” said Rep. Rosa DeLauro (Conn.), the senior Democrat on the House Appropriations Committee. That internal clash has been playing out for several weeks on the other side of the Capitol, where Senate Democrats are also at odds over how aggressively to pursue the defund-the-war strategy in the lame duck session — a debate that’s grown only more salient after Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) launched a challenge to Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) for the top leadership spot next year. Van Hollen has positioned himself to the left of Schumer, and his demand to halt war funding immediately — even if it leads to a government shutdown — has energized the Democrats’ liberal base even as it has divided the party on Capitol Hill.

items.excerpt: ## Sunrise on the Reaping sets the biggest UK opening day of 2026 The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping took $8.2 million on its opening day in the UK, the biggest of 2026 so far, passing Spider-Man: Brand New Day at $7.8 million, Fiction Horizon reports. It had already taken $21 million in Thursday previews in the US, and ScreenRant projects more than $120 million domestic for the opening weekend as of Saturday morning, with final numbers due Monday. Yesterday’s roundup carried the $51 million Friday projection; our reviews piece has the critics split at 67% on Rotten Tomatoes. ## O.M Chapter 1 opens with Rs 19.75 crore in India on day 1 O.M Chapter 1 opened with Rs 19.75 crore in India on day 1, 20 November 2026, Dhanush’s biggest opener, Pinkvilla reports from trade estimates. Production house Wunderbar Films announced over Rs 40 crore worldwide gross on day 1. ## Helen Fraser dies aged 84 Helen Fraser, best known as Bad Girls prison officer Sylvia Hollamby in all eight series, has died aged 84, The Sun reports. ... ## Robin Varghese dies aged 56 Robin Varghese, the Malayalam actor known as Shelly in the 1992 Mammootty film Johny Walker, has died aged 56, the Times of India reports from Manorama Online, with NewsBytes also reporting the death. He died in the United States on 19 November 2026. No cause of death was given. ... ## Onslaught streams on HBO Max from 22 December A24’s Onslaught streams on HBO Max from 22 December 2026, ScreenRant reports, after its 4 September 2026 theatrical run and 6 October 2026 digital debut. The date was announced on 20 November 2026. ## Mission: Cross 2 sets a December 2026 Netflix window Mission: Cross 2 has set a December 2026 Netflix release window after a delay from its Q3 2026 slot, What’s on Netflix reports. Hwang Jung Min and Yeom Jung Ah return, with four cast additions, and no exact date has been announced. ... ## Bhogi locks a 27 November release date Sharwanand film Bhogi has locked a new worldwide release date of 27 November 2026, Gulte reports, after the CBFC revising committee cleared it with an A certificate. The makers announced the date on 19 November 2026 after its 12 November release was postponed, with a trailer launch and pre-release event reported for today, 22 November.

items.title: Reuters Entertainment News Summary | International
items.excerpt: Saudi Arabia once banned Grand Theft Auto. Now it's got a stake ​in it Grand Theft Auto, banned in Saudi Arabia until last year, is now being ​embraced not only by its gamers - a category that includes ‌Crown ​Prince Mohammed bin Salman - but also by its sovereign wealth fund, which the prince chairs. This week, gamers in Saudi Arabia joined legions of fans around the world to play Grand Theft Auto VI upon launch — the first new release of the top-selling series since a ‌Saudi ban was scrapped in 2025. GTA VI shatters records with $3.8 billion in first-day sales "Grand Theft Auto VI" raked in $3.79 billion in sales within the first 24 hours of its launch, becoming the world's biggest entertainment release ever, as fans around the world celebrated the blockbuster title that is now a global cultural phenomenon. The action-adventure title that sees criminal duo Lucia and Jason blitz through the ‌neon-soaked streets of Vice City sold 32.5 million units pre-release, developer Rockstar Games said on Friday, a day after the game launched to massive fanfare and critical acclaim globally. French actor ‌Depardieu and author Houellebecq under investigation for sexual assault The Paris prosecutor's office said on Saturday it had opened a judicial investigation into actor Gerard Depardieu and author Michel Houellebecq over alleged sexual offences after a legal complaint was filed against them. AFP News agency reported on Friday that the men had been jointly accused of the gang rape and assault of a woman during a 2018 film shoot ... Miley Cyrus weds drummer Maxx Morando in California, People magazine reports Grammy-winning pop star ​Miley Cyrus married her longtime partner, drummer Maxx Morando, in California on Saturday, People magazine and other US entertainment news outlets reported. Cyrus and Morando reportedly tied the knot ⁠at a private ceremony in Palm Springs, a month after performing "Let's Get Married" together at the Hollywood Bowl. The song appears on Cyrus' latest studio album, Bass Persuades.
